section_name: Unit 1: Python Basics: Variables, Data Types & Operators
description: Declare and use variables following Python naming conventions. Work with int, float, str, bool. Apply arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators. Use type conversion and f-string formatting.

lessons.title: Core Concepts: Variables & Data Types
lessons.html_content:
Amazon's recommendation engine — the system behind 'Customers also bought…' — starts with product data: IDs (int), prices (float), names (str), availability (bool).

Key Concepts

  • Variables: containers for data (int, float, str, bool, NoneType)
  • Naming: snake_case, descriptive, no reserved words
  • Arithmetic: + − * / // % ** (floor div, modulo, power)
  • Comparison operators: == != > < >= <= (return bool)
  • Type conversion: int() float() str() bool()
  • f-strings: f'Product: {name}, Price: ${price:.2f}'

Amazon Product Data Example

product_id     = 101
product_name   = "Wireless Headphones"
price          = 49.99
in_stock       = True
discount_pct   = 0.15
discounted     = price * (1 - discount_pct)
print(f"Price: ${price:.2f}")
print(f"Discounted: ${discounted:.2f}")

lessons.title: Coding Practice: Variables
lessons.html_content:
Exercise 1: Product Listing

Create variables for 3 Amazon products (id, name, price, in_stock). Print a formatted listing for each using f-strings with 2 decimal places for prices.

Exercise 2: Price Calculator

Build a discount calculator: input original_price and discount_percent, output final_price and savings. Use round() for precision.

Exercise 3: String Manipulator

Take a product name as input. Print it in UPPER, lower, and Title Case. Count characters with len(). Check if 'pro' appears in the name.

lessons.title: Reference Readings: Built-in Types
lessons.html_content:
Recommended Reading

  1. Python Built-in Types — docs.python.org — Complete reference for all built-in Python types.
  2. Real Python: Variables in Python — realpython.com — Practical guide with common mistakes to avoid.
  3. f-Strings: Improved String Formatting — realpython.com — f-strings are the standard in all modern Python codebases.

assignment.title: Amazon Product Price Tracker
assignment.instructions:
Amazon's pricing team monitors price changes across millions of products. Build a mini price-tracker simulating this logic.

Tasks:
1. Define 5 products as variables: name, original_price, discount_pct
2. Calculate and display: discounted price, savings, and a DEAL label if savings > 20%
3. Format output in aligned columns with 2 decimal places
4. Calculate and print total cart value at the bottom

forum.title: Unit 1 Discussion
forum.prompt: Amazon tracks hundreds of product attributes per listing. If you were designing a Python-based product catalog, what data types would you assign to: rating, number of reviews, prime eligibility, seller name, and delivery date? Explain your choices in 150–200 words. Reply to 2 peers and suggest one type they may have reconsidered.
